name: tabor-elemental-charge
title: Elemental charge
description: Explore electric charge and connect the physical examples to Nathan Tabor’s project.
sections: A proton carries one positive elementary charge, an electron one negative elementary charge, and a neutron is electrically neutral. An ion’s net charge in elementary-charge units is the proton count minus the electron count.
Ion concentration gradients and membrane permeability contribute to the electrical potential across cell membranes. Sodium, potassium and chloride are examples of ions with roles in that process.
The original puts elemental charge beside the artifacts, nature and the human body. A correspondence can be indexed by the element or ion, its observable behavior and its role in the story.
Neutral sodium has 11 protons and 11 electrons. Na⁺ has the same 11 protons and 10 electrons. The proton count fixes the element and the balance of the two particle counts fixes the net charge.
